extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing manuscripts for submission to Geometry & Topology Monographs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting research articles to the Geometry & Topology Monographs series, including language, file/format expectations, references, figures, and proof-handling. Targets final-production requirements (LaTeX) as well as initial submission practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: The normal language used by the journal is English, but articles written in other languages are acceptable, provided the monograph editor is happy with the language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your chosen language is not English, then an additional English version of your abstract is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial submission format flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For submission purposes you can prepare your article in any way which suits you and is acceptable to the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may submit initial manuscripts in any format acceptable to the editor; exact production formatting is not required for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX requirement for accepted papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Once accepted for publication, the paper must be prepared in some flavour of LaTeX, preferably using the journal's prepared class file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the provided LaTeX instructions for preparing articles in LaTeX for publication in gtm; using the series' class file is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: References: alphabetical listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographical references should be listed alphabetically at the end of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any bibliographical citation style may be used on submission, but references will be converted to the house style (see a current issue for examples). Use of BibTeX is preferred but not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: References must be cited in text
rubrics_metrics.description: All references in the bibliography should be cited at least once in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure quality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures, whether prepared electronically or hand-drawn, must be of publication quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clarity and appropriate resolution so figures reproduce well in print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable electronic figure formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures prepared electronically should be submitted in Encapsulated PostScript (EPS) or Portable Document Format (PDF) or in a form that can be converted to one of these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable convertible sources include GnuPlot, Maple, Mathematica, or XFig. Many drawing tools such as Inkscape, Adobe Illustrator and Aldus FreeHand can produce EPS or PDF output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bitmap figure resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures containing bitmaps should be generated at the highest possible resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is doubt whether a particular figure is in an acceptable format, authors should check with production by emailing graphics@msp.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs and author responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Page proofs will be made available to authors (or to the designated corresponding author) at a Web site in PDF format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to acknowledge receipt of proofs or to return corrections within the requested deadline may cause publication to be postponed.
